title: A Study on Efficiency Improvements of DNN Accelerators via Denormalized Arithmetic Elimination
problem: DNN accelerators use reduced precision floating-point (RPF) formats like bfloat16 and TensorFloat32 for efficiency, but supporting denormalized number handling adds complexity without contributing to DNN inference accuracy.
motivation: Denormalized floating-point arithmetic adds circuit complexity for minimal benefit in DNN inference. Eliminating this support can reduce area, power, and critical path while maintaining classification accuracy.
method: Analysis of denormalized number impact on DNN inference accuracy across vision and speech tasks. Hardware multiplier designs with and without denormalized arithmetic support compared in terms of area, delay, and power.
key_novelty: Demonstrates that eliminating denormalized arithmetic support from GEMM hardware does not affect DNN classification accuracy while enabling significant efficiency gains.
contributions: Analysis of denormalized number impact on DNN accuracy
46% area reduction (LUT count) by removing denormalized support
Applicability to reduced precision formats in ML accelerators
Implications for power efficiency in data centers
limitations: Study focused on arithmetic units; system-level integration and impact on full accelerator design not explored. Limited to specific RPF formats (bfloat16, TensorFloat32).
